Foreign Affairs
Cr. & Sp. Branch
U. 586
11-10-44
October 7, 1944.
K
KNOX, John Frederick, British subject -
attempted suicide and attempted murder.

Preliminary investigations conducted by the undersigned
ascertained the following:
John Frederick Knox, Eurasian, British subject, married;
age 36, formerly employed by the Shanghai Gas Co., residing
with his wife, of Chinese origin, and two sons, John, 10 years
old, and Kenneth, 9 years old, at 656 Yu Ya Ching Rd., was
exempted from internment on account of complete blindness.
He lost the sight of his eyes about 6 years ago when he was a
assaulted by a Chinese employee of the Gas Co. by throwing
acid into his face, whilst he (Mr.Knox) was on the company's
service. On account of this Mr.Knox was made pensioner of
the Gas Co., and was allowed by the Japanese Authorities
to reside in the company's quarters at the above address.
During the last few days Mr.Knox is stated to be
in very depressed state of conditions, and members of the
family were living in the fear for his mental stability.
About 2 a.m., on 6.10.44, Mr.Knox woke up his
family, and after prolonged arguments persuaded them to
commit suicide by cutting veins on their hands. Having taken
possession of a razor blade he inflicted cuts on the left
wrists of his wife and both sons, all of whom though protes-
ting against it offered very week resistance. After that Mr.
Knox cut the veins on both his wrists, continuing to repeat
that he must end his life.
However, injuries inflicted did not turn
out to be serious enough to threaten the life in either
case, and Mr.Knox and his family, probably realizing what
has been done, were apparently trying to hide the fact.
On the same morning (6.10.44) about 11 o'clock
Mr.Knox, accompanied by his elder son, John, visited the

K
诺克斯，约翰·弗雷德里克（John Frederick Knox），英国臣民——
企图自杀及企图谋杀。

经下述签署人进行的初步调查，查明情况如下：
约翰·弗雷德里克·诺克斯，欧亚混血儿，英国臣民，已婚；
36岁，前受雇于上海煤气公司，与其中国籍妻子及两个儿子（10岁的约翰和9岁的肯尼斯）居住在愚园路656号，因完全失明而被免除拘禁。
约6年前，当诺克斯先生为公司服务时，遭一名煤气公司华籍雇员向其面部泼洒硫酸，导致双目失明。因此，诺克斯先生成为煤气公司的领取养老金者，并获日本当局许可居住在上述地址的公司宿舍内。
据称，在过去几天里，诺克斯先生情绪极度低落，其家人生活在对其精神稳定性的恐惧之中。
1944年10月6日凌晨2点左右，诺克斯先生唤醒家人，经过长时间争论后，说服他们割腕自杀。他拿到一片剃须刀片后，割伤了他妻子和两个儿子的左手腕，尽管他们表示反对，但抵抗非常微弱。随后，诺克斯先生割伤了自己的双腕，并不断重复说他必须结束自己的生命。
然而，所造成的伤害在任何情况下均不足以危及生命，诺克斯先生及其家人可能意识到所发生之事，显然试图隐瞒这一事实。
同日（1944年10月6日）上午11点左右，诺克斯先生在其长子约翰的陪同下前往

Swiss Consulate General regarding relief money, and returned
home without informing any one of the occurrence. Neither of
the family went to see any doctor.
At about 2 p.m., on 6.10.44, a missionary, brother
John, Irish (other particulars unknown at present) came to
see Mr.Knox at his home and on discovering the situation
immediately informed the Swiss Consulate General. Mr.Stutz,
in charge of British Section of the Swiss Consulate General
arrived, after which brother John accompanied the two boys
to the General Hospital where they were attended to by
Dr.Smolnikoff and Dr.Andreeff.
After having some arguments with Mr.Knox, who would
not like to go to the hospital, Mr.Stutz went to the tele-
phone leaving Mr.Knox alone. The latter took this opportunity
and jumped through the window from the forth floor falling
on the roof of an adjoining building. He was taken in an ambu-
lance to the General Hospital where he was attended to by
Dr.Danziger, and was found suffering from fracture of left
leg and cuts on both wrists. Dr.Danziger opined that, though
there were no definite indications, yet it was most probably
that attempt on his life and lifes of his family was committed
by Mr.Knox in a state of "temporary insanity".
Mrs.Knox seems to have received the slightest
injuries of all. She visited General Hospital only on next
day (7.10.44) and was attended to by Dr.Smolnikoff, after which
which she went home.
Mr.Knox was visited by the undersigned in the
hospital at 9.30 a.m., 7.10.44, and stated that he would not
make any statement to the Police before he consults with the
Swiss Consulate's officials.
When asked by the undersigned regarding reasons
for his attempt on his life and lifes of his family, Mr.Knox
stated that he was disappointed and disgusted with the life,
and wanted his family to die with him to safe them from
further sufferings. He also stated that many of his old

瑞士总领事馆商讨救济金事宜，回家后未向任何人透露此事。家中无人去看医生。
1944年10月6日下午2点左右，一位爱尔兰传教士约翰兄弟（John，其他详情目前不详）来到诺克斯先生家中探望，发现情况后立即通知了瑞士总领事馆。负责瑞士总领事馆英国部事务的斯塔茨先生（Mr. Stutz）抵达后，约翰兄弟陪同两名男孩前往广慈医院（General Hospital），由斯莫尔尼科夫医生（Dr. Smolnikoff）和安德烈夫医生（Dr. Andreeff）进行诊治。
斯塔茨先生与不愿去医院的诺克斯先生发生了一些争执后，留下诺克斯先生独自一人在场，自己去打电话。后者利用这一机会，从四楼跳窗而出，落在相邻建筑的屋顶上。他被救护车送往广慈医院，由丹齐格医生（Dr. Danziger）诊治，发现其左腿骨折且双腕有割伤。丹齐格医生认为，虽然没有确凿迹象，但诺克斯先生对自己及家人生命的侵害极有可能是在“暂时性精神错乱”状态下实施的。
诺克斯太太似乎受伤最轻。她仅在次日（1944年10月7日）前往广慈医院，由斯莫尔尼科夫医生诊治后回家。
下述签署人于1944年10月7日上午9点30分在医院探访了诺克斯先生，他表示在咨询瑞士领事馆官员之前，不会向警方做任何陈述。
当被问及企图杀害自己及家人的原因时，诺克斯先生称他对生活感到失望和厌恶，希望家人与他同死，以使她们免受进一步的痛苦。他还表示，他的许多老

friends were looking upon him with disdain, suspecting him
of being secretly connected with the Japanese authorities.
This suspicion, he stated was based on the fact that he
was exempted from internment and was living in the Gas
company's quarters. This suspicion, he said, was intolerable
for him and he decided to end his life. Besides, he pointed
out, being a blind man he did not expect that he might ever
enjoy the life.

V. Mutaevsky
D.S.I.

朋友都轻视他，怀疑他与日本当局有秘密联系。
他说，这种怀疑是基于他被免除拘禁并居住在煤气公司宿舍这一事实。他说，这种怀疑对他来说是无法忍受的，因此他决定结束自己的生命。此外，他指出，作为一个盲人，他不指望自己能享受生活。

V. 穆塔耶夫斯基（V. Mutaevsky）
